## Overview Reject `canonical_layout=true` for the default or explicitly selected `CPUOffloadingSpec`, with an actionable startup error instead of accepting an option its worker does not implement. Preserve `TieringOffloadingSpec` support and correct the usage guide. Addresses the configuration-contract subtask in #63718; the broader tracking issue remains open. ## Claims - Validate the normalized flag during CPU-spec construction, before allocating offload memory. The error suggests selecting `TieringOffloadingSpec` or removing the option. - Keep omitted/false settings and Tiering canonical settings valid, including Tiering with only a CPU primary tier. - Add factory and real-`LLM` startup regressions, select the latter in the active KV Offload CI step, and document the actual support boundary. ## Validation Local environment: macOS arm64, Python 3.14.6, PyTorch 2.13.0, native CPU extensions built from this checkout with Apple Clang 15.0.0. - New factory regression on the base implementation: **2 failed** with `DID NOT RAISE`; control cases: 5 passed. - Factory, file-mapper, tiering and connector-config suites after the change: **207 passed**. - Real OPT-125m `LLM` startup regression, omitted and explicit CPU spec: **2 passed**. On the base implementation, the macOS run reaches the pre-existing GPU-only offload restriction instead of the specific canonical-layout error; this validates configuration rejection ordering, not GPU data transfer. - Real OPT-125m FP32 CPU generation smoke: loaded checkpoint weights, created KV cache and generated 8 greedy tokens successfully. - Changed-file `pre-commit run --files ...`: all applicable hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy, Markdown and Buildkite test selection checks. Reproduction commands, using the configured virtual environment: ```bash uv run --no-project .venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider \ tests/v1/kv_offload/test_factory.py \ tests/v1/kv_offload/test_file_mapper.py \ tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py -q GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo0 VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 \ uv run --no-project .venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider \ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py \ -k test_cpu_offloading_rejects_canonical_layout -v ``` `lo0` is the macOS loopback interface; omit or adapt it on other hosts. CUDA/ROCm startup and GPU-to-CPU transfer validation were not run locally. This change does not alter model math or the load/store implementation. ## Details `build_offloading_config` preserves the requested canonical flag for either spec, but only Tiering forwards it to `CPUOffloadingWorker`. CPU construction now checks an inherited private capability; Tiering opts in, so the shared constructor does not reject its supported path. CPU subclasses inherit rejection unless they explicitly implement and opt into canonical support. Duplicate-work check on 2026-10-26: no overlapping open PR was found by issue-number and canonical-layout/CPU-spec searches. #60005 handles LHBNC registration and #62566 handles secondary-tier topology warnings. AI assistance (Codex) was used for implementation, investigation and local validation. ---

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

The unsupported CPU configuration should fail, and the docs/startup coverage look appropriate. I’d prefer to handle this through spec-specific extra-config validation, following the model-loader pattern, rather than introducing a capability flag for each unsupported option. Please preserve explicit false/default CPU settings and Tiering canonical support.

Can we validate the selected spec’s extra config here, following `DefaultModelLoader` / `RunaiModelStreamerLoader`, instead of adding `_supports_canonical_layout`? They check supported keys and then values/combinations. CPU should still accept omitted/false canonical layout and reject true. Please account for shared connector options and let Tiering/custom specs extend the validation.

 | `sync_load_budget_bytes` | no | `0` | both | Per-step budget of KV bytes (per GPU) loaded within the same step, so those requests run immediately instead of waiting a step for an async load. Hits that don't fit the remaining budget, or would leave nothing to compute, stay async. `0` disables. |
 | `self_describing_kv_events` | no | `false` | both | Opt-in. When `true` *and* KV cache events are enabled (`--kv-events-config` with `enable_kv_cache_events`), the connector emits self-describing block-granular `BlockStored`/`BlockRemoved` payloads (constituent block hashes, whole-chunk `token_ids`, per-block `block_size`, parent hash, LoRA + group/cache-spec metadata) instead of the placeholder fallback, so external KV-event consumers can index offloaded blocks. Inert unless events are enabled. With `TieringOffloadingSpec`, a CPU promotion is self-describing when a local request observes its primary-tier `HIT` before event translation; otherwise its stored event may retain the placeholder, while a later `HIT` can backfill metadata for removal. Pending-removal/re-promotion races and externally initiated promotions may also produce placeholders, and consumers must ignore removals for unknown hashes. Partial recurrent tails emit the hash-aligned portion from the physical block start through the tail boundary. Other sliding-window/SSM chunks keep the placeholder fallback. In chunk mode (`block_size` > GPU block size, or `blocks_per_chunk` > 1), overlapping chunks re-announce shared per-block hashes, so consumers must reference-count (deduplicate) repeated store/remove announcements. |
 | `spec_module_path` | no | — | both | Python import path for a custom `OffloadingSpec` not in the built-in registry. Required only when `spec_name` is not built-in (advanced). |
-| `canonical_layout` | no | `false` | both | Store each offloaded block in a common canonical representation instead of each worker's local GPU page (enables sharing across TP sizes and single-copy storage of replicated KV). See [Canonical Layout](#canonical-layout). |
+| `canonical_layout` | no | `false` | multi-tier | Requires `TieringOffloadingSpec`. Store each offloaded block in a common canonical representation instead of each worker's local GPU page (enables sharing across TP sizes and single-copy storage of replicated KV). See [Canonical Layout](#canonical-layout). |
 
 ## Canonical Layout
 
 By default, each worker copies its own GPU page to the CPU tier unchanged, so an offloaded block is stored in whatever form that worker happens to hold it.
 
-With `"canonical_layout": true`, workers instead convert their local pages into one common representation, the canonical page: the block's complete KV (every KV head and every token), with each worker writing its slice into a fixed position. The format is versioned and doesn't depend on how a particular engine splits the KV across its workers.
+With `"spec_name": "TieringOffloadingSpec"` and `"canonical_layout": true`, workers instead convert their local pages into one common representation, the canonical page: the block's complete KV (every KV head and every token), with each worker writing its slice into a fixed position. The format is versioned and doesn't depend on how a particular engine splits the KV across its workers.
+
+`CPUOffloadingSpec` (the default when `spec_name` is omitted) rejects `canonical_layout: true` at startup. Use `TieringOffloadingSpec` to enable canonical layout, or leave `canonical_layout` disabled for `CPUOffloadingSpec`. Secondary tiers are optional: `TieringOffloadingSpec` also supports canonical layout with only its CPU primary tier.
 
 Having a single, well-defined representation enables several things:
